title: Climate Change and Global Warming
text: Global warming refers specifically to the long-term heating of Earth's surface since the pre-industrial period (1850–1900), driven primarily by human activities, especially burning fossil fuels. The global average temperature has risen about 1.1°C above pre-industrial levels. Effects include increased frequency of extreme weather events, sea level rise, melting of Arctic sea ice and glaciers, shifting precipitation patterns, and threats to biodiversity. The Paris Agreement (2015) set a goal to limit warming to 1.5°C or well below 2°C above pre-industrial levels. Climate models project that without significant emissions reduction, global temperatures could rise 2–4°C or more by 2100, with severe consequences for ecosystems and human civilization.
